A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AVGGT work. All 23 pages of each version, including appendix tables and attention visualizations, are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation, point-map, runtime, and ablation results for AVGGT and its π3 adaptation, including additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds ETH3D evaluation, query-subsampling ablations, and FLOP measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed early global-to-frame conversion and uniform K/V subsampling retain the same layer thresholds, reference-frame treatment, diagonal preservation, and mean component. The new query-subsampling variants are diagnostic ablations; the proposed inference procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds camera-pose evaluation on ETH3D in appendix Table 8. RealEstate10K, TUM-dynamics, DTU, 7-Scenes, Sintel, ScanNet, and NRGBD remain, with no removal of existing task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 11 evaluates two additional comparison variants, AVGGT(2+Q2Near) and AVGGT(2+Q2GM), against VGGT and AVGGT(4). External benchmark baselines and Faster configurations remain unchanged; ETH3D reuses the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: Tables 1–5 add FLOPs as an efficiency metric, and Section 9.2 introduces a roughly compute-matched query-subsampling comparison. The reported VGGT encoder training status changes from frozen to fine-tuned, without establishing retraining or rerunning existing experiments. Existing sequence lengths and accuracy metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Section 9.2 and new Table 11 test whether queries can also be subsampled. Nearest-query and global-mean approximations achieve AUC@30 of 78.310 and 68.382, versus 87.045 for AVGGT(4). Existing layer, sampling, diagonal, reference-frame, and rotation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run uncertainty. Existing mean/median metric reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds ETH3D scores, query-ablation outcomes, and FLOP values. Table 1 revises AVGGT(4)'s AUC@5/15/30 from 55.570/76.675/85.446 to 59.583/79.188/87.045, matching the existing Table 6 ablation. Table 4 changes Faster π3_75 runtime from 32.492 to 23.146 seconds. These are bounded additions and corrections; most matched results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Token definitions, subsampling factorization, and computational-complexity expressions retain their mathematical content. Notation is standardized, but no new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the peak-speedup claim into approximate context-length claims: 2× at 100 frames, 4–5× at 300, and 8–10× at 800. The central attention-role analysis, training-free acceleration contribution, and accuracy-preservation claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the frozen-encoder explanation with a tentative argument that fine-tuning may insufficiently reshape features for 3D reasoning. Sections 4.3 and 9.2 add the interpretation that query subsampling reduces token diversity, explaining the larger degradation from global-mean queries.

D1.justification: v2 revises the documented VGGT encoder training status, explicitly identifies the stride pairs in Section 4.3 as the settings used, and describes how the new query-ablation variants approximate skipped queries. Hardware and FlashAttention-2 information remain unchanged; no code-access disclosure is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Schöps et al. ETH3D benchmark citation. The positioning relative to DUSt3R, VGGT, π3, FastVGGT, and FasterVGGT remains substantially unchanged. Other reference edits mainly update formatting and bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and explanatory revisions, standardizes notation and terminology, and updates corresponding-author details, acknowledgments, and bibliography formatting. The main section sequence and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–5 gain FLOP columns and frame-count captions. Two new appendix tables cause renumbering and local reflow. Several main figures are re-rendered, while the existing attention visualizations and ablation plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: FLOP reporting, ETH3D evaluation, and the query-subsampling ablation strengthen support for the existing method. Table 1 now agrees with the retained ablation results, and the encoder explanation is qualified. These benefits outweigh a limited new inconsistency: Figure 1 still plots the earlier Faster π3_75 runtime despite Table 4's revision. The overall improvement is useful but bounded.
